clue.text: Musical instrument neighbour brought round

indicators.note: bringing something round turns it to face the other way, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: to neighbour something is to abut it, sharing a border

explanation.surface: A neighbour drops by carrying a big brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neighbour' is a verb here, not the person next door.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the largest, lowest-pitched brass instrument in an orchestra, so it is one example of the category.

clue.text: The Spanish club climbing league list?

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A Spanish football club rises up the league standings.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a description: the standings of a sports league are set out in a ranked grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A league table is the ranked chart of teams and points, so a list of a league's standings is that chart.

clue.text: Variable rent around good London area

indicators.note: rent here is the past tense of rend, meaning torn apart, so the letters before it are ripped up and rearranged
around tells you the rearranged letters go about another piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Rents in a smart part of London go up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable rent' reads as a fluctuating housing cost, but rent is the anagram signal and variable is the fodder. Belgravia is an expensive district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgravia is a wealthy residential district in central London, near Hyde Park, so it is an instance of a London area.

clue.text: Lawyer has drink with secret society member

blocks.note: perry is an alcoholic drink made from pears
a Freemason, member of a famously secretive fraternity; 'with' joins it on

explanation.surface: A lawyer shares a drink with a Freemason.
explanation.walkthrough: Perry is the pear equivalent of cider.
explanation.definitionFit: Perry Mason is the fictional defence attorney of Erle Stanley Gardner's novels and the long-running television series.

clue.text: Rodent leading with its tail, and not really big

indicators.note: the creature's final letter goes first, so its last letter is moved round to the front

blocks.note: a mouse is a small rodent
nor means 'and not'

explanation.surface: A rodent walks backwards, yet is not actually very big.
explanation.walkthrough: With its last letter moved to the front the rodent is split after that letter, and 'and not' slots in straight after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous is a stronger synonym of huge; something really big in size fits the adjective exactly.

clue.text: Mounted equipment restricting noise

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece keeps another confined within it

blocks.note: a rig is a set of equipment, as in a drilling or sound rig
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Equipment fitted on a mount that muffles noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' looks like it describes the equipment; it is the definition, as in a person seated on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mounted is on horseback, and riding describes a person seated on and travelling on a horse.

clue.text: I won't give away a spy working with Emerald Isle

indicators.note: working letters are in motion and being reshaped, so these words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An agent operating in Ireland refuses to divulge anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emerald Isle is a nickname for Ireland, but here its letters are fodder along with 'a spy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a promise of secrecy, a declaration that the speaker will not reveal a confidence.

clue.text: Some hairy slob up country

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, a run of consecutive letters
in a down entry, up means the letters run from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: the run of letters sits across the two words, from the second letter of the first

explanation.surface: A hairy slob is cheering on his country.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, the letters straddle the end of hairy and the start of slob.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East, bordering Lebanon, Turkey and Iraq.

clue.text: Iron structure in sunset horribly hot inside

indicators.note: horribly suggests a mess, so the preceding letters are jumbled
inside tells you one piece is placed within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A metal building gets unbearably hot as the sun sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a prefabricated semicircular shelter made of corrugated iron, used widely in wartime.

clue.text: Item subject to inflation in Lebanese port

blocks.note: first meaning: a rubber wheel covering that is pumped up with air
second meaning: an ancient Phoenician city on the coast of Lebanon

explanation.surface: Prices are rising in a Lebanese harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' suggests rising prices in an economy, but it means pumping up with air.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre is filled with compressed air; separately, Tyre is a coastal city in southern Lebanon.

clue.text: Owl old boy trained for film industry

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An owl trained by a former pupil is headed for the movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boy' looks like a unit meaning a former pupil, but both words are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bollywood is the nickname for the Hindi-language cinema business based in Mumbai.

clue.text: Large chests in small singers?

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
an ark is an old word for a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Big chests packed into tiny choristers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: these songbirds are small and famous for singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Larks are small songbirds noted for their song in flight, so they are little birds that sing.

clue.text: High place where Providence is in view

indicators.note: is in places one piece within another, enclosed by it

blocks.note: to eye something is to view it
Providence is the capital of Rhode Island, abbreviated RI

explanation.surface: A lofty spot from which divine Providence can be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Providence looks like divine guidance; it stands for its US state, Rhode Island, by its postal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built on a crag, and figuratively any lofty, remote dwelling.

clue.text: Frenchman Napoleon crashed an aircraft

indicators.note: something that crashed has been smashed up, so the name's letters are broken and reassembled

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a French man
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The French emperor Napoleon crashes a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frenchman Napoleon' reads as one person, but Frenchman supplies only its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A monoplane is a fixed-wing aeroplane with a single pair of wings, so it is one kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Snooker champ winning after century in competition

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the one it follows in the answer

blocks.note: Steve Davis, six-time world snooker champion in the 1980s
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a side that is up is ahead, winning

explanation.surface: A snooker champion scores a century break to win a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: A century is a familiar snooker break of 100 points, which strengthens the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Davis Cup is the premier international team tournament in men's tennis.

clue.text: Small storm: Luddites upset about verse

indicators.note: upset means overturned and thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
V is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: Machine-breaking Luddites cause a minor storm with angry poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Luddites were 19th-century textile workers who smashed machinery; their name is only fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust devil is a small whirlwind that lifts dust and debris, a miniature localised storm.

clue.text: Chap who wrote Rocket Man did you say?

indicators.note: asking whether you said something points to how a word is heard rather than written

blocks.note: George Stephenson, engineer of the Rocket steam locomotive of 1829

explanation.surface: Who wrote the song Rocket Man, you ask?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocket Man' calls up Elton John's song, but it is the railway engineer whose locomotive was the Rocket. The author is Robert Louis Stevenson.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island and Kidnapped, so the surname belongs to a famous writer.

clue.text: Operatic song in pub for social outcast

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second, which wraps around it

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: An opera singer belting out a song in the pub is shunned by the other drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: PH marks pubs on British Ordnance Survey maps.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is a person rejected and avoided by society, so an outcast.

clue.text: Party not now held by island pagans?

indicators.note: held by means gripped from outside, so these letters sit inside the next piece

blocks.note: a do is a party or celebration
not now means at some later time
Is. is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A party postponed while held on an island of heathens.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that not every pagan worships idols: the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolaters worship idols or images, which monotheists have traditionally condemned as heathen practice.

clue.text: My husband carried in pleasant Rolls-Royce

indicators.note: something carried in another is held inside it, so these letters go within

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for husband, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A wife boasts that her husband was driven about in a pleasant Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is an exclamation; cor is a British expression of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Corniche was a luxury convertible and coupe model built by Rolls-Royce from 1971.

clue.text: See 6
Primary timber source outside Missouri

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes around the second, enclosing it

blocks.note: a forest supplies wood for timber
MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri

explanation.surface: The main source of timber lies outside Missouri.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost means first in rank or importance, the same sense as chief or principal.

clue.text: Is he bound to miss?

blocks.note: surface reading: is this man certain to fail to hit the target?
setter's reading: a man promised in marriage to a Miss, an unmarried woman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'sure to', and 'miss' like failing to hit; read instead 'bound' as pledged and 'Miss' as a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A man engaged to be married is pledged to his bride-to-be, a woman still addressed as Miss.

clue.text: Desperate fellow, drunk, sent back new wine variety

indicators.note: something sent back goes the way it came, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: Desperate Dan, a strongman cowboy in the British children's comic The Dandy
oiled is slang for drunk
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A desperate drunk sends back a new wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a famous comic-strip character from The Dandy, a British children's comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandelion wine is a homemade country wine brewed from the flower's petals, one variety among many.

clue.text: Rules indoors most regularly ignored

indicators.note: every other letter is passed over at regular intervals, keeping the rest

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Indoor rules are mostly disregarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Norms are accepted standards of behaviour, the conventions a group expects members to follow.

clue.text: Ray quiet at the back

blocks.note: sh is the instruction to be quiet
aft is the nautical term for towards the stern, the back

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray keeps quiet at the back of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a person's name; it is the definition, a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of light is a beam, so shaft and ray are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Problem with pressure in oil receptacle

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
P is the symbol for pressure; 'with' joins it on

explanation.surface: A pressure problem in the engine's oil system.
explanation.definitionFit: The sump is the reservoir at the bottom of an engine's crankcase where lubricating oil collects.

clue.text: Express disapproval with our heartless teacher

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is taken out, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: tut is a click of the tongue showing disapproval
the first and last letters of 'our'; 'with' joins it on

explanation.surface: Pupils grumble about their cold-hearted teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private instructor or university teacher who guides students individually.

clue.text: Unwelcome invader's flying bomb surge endless

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the V-1 was the German flying bomb of the Second World War, written VI
a rush is a sudden surge

explanation.surface: An enemy invader's flying bombs come in an unending surge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus invades the body's cells uninvited and causes disease, so it is an intruder nobody wants.

clue.text: Turned on married men getting into bed? 6 Down 19 Across!

indicators.note: turned means faced the other way, so the next word is read backwards
getting into means entering, so these letters go inside another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a cot is a small bed
M is the abbreviation for married
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandal about married men caught in bed draws a tight-lipped response.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 6 Down and 19 Across, a phrase that also refuses to divulge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are ways of declining to say anything, the stock reply of someone refusing to disclose.

clue.text: City's battered galleons are French

indicators.note: battered means knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
es is French for 'are' in tu es, you are

explanation.surface: A city's battered old warships turn out to be French.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Angeles is the largest city in California, so it is a city in the plainest sense.

clue.text: Addict taken in because relapsed

indicators.note: taken in means held within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run starts in the last three letters of the first word and ends on the first of the second

explanation.surface: An addict is admitted to rehab because of a relapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relapsed' tempts you to reverse something, but the letters run forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for a drug taker, so it is a synonym of an addict.
